clue.text: Blocked, having troubled doubts etc about runs

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disordered, so the words that follow are rearranged
about means going around, so the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone stuck because they are fretting over doubts and other worries about runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of 'doubts etc' rearrange to OBSTUCTED, and R slips in after OBST to make OBSTRUCTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstructed and blocked are plain synonyms, both meaning prevented from moving or progressing.

clue.text: Well up in waste resinous stuff of use to insects

definitions.text: resinous stuff of use to insects

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is written bottom to top, in reverse
in says the turned word sits inside the next word

blocks.note: gee and well are both exclamations of mild surprise
to blue money is British slang for squandering it

explanation.surface: A spring wells up in a wasteland, bringing up a resin that insects find useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well up' reads as a spring rising, but it is an exclamation turned over. Bee glue is another name for propolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Bee glue, or propolis, is the resinous substance bees collect from buds to seal and repair their hives.

clue.text: Far from merry widow who can be fully gratified? Not able

indicators.note: not able tells us to take away the letters spelling able from the word before

blocks.note: satiable means capable of being satisfied

explanation.surface: A widow far from merry wonders who could ever satisfy her completely, finding nobody able.
explanation.walkthrough: Sati was the Hindu widow who burned herself on her husband's funeral pyre, so 'far from merry' plays on The Merry Widow, Lehar's operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A sati is a Hindu widow who sacrificed herself on her husband's pyre, the grimmest contrast with a merry one.

clue.text: Work left when climbing? It's too much

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means going up the column, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: OP, short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A climber complains that the effort left over is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Troppo is the Italian musical direction meaning too much, as in allegro ma non troppo.

clue.text: Copy penned by mature professional

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of mature and the start of professional

explanation.surface: An imitation document written by an experienced expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Repro is a short form of reproduction, a replica or duplicate of an original.

clue.text: Face to Face, story about Father getting tipsy

indicators.note: about means going round, so the story wraps round what follows

blocks.note: a conte is a short story, from French
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
on can mean slightly drunk, as in a bit on

explanation.surface: A review of the film Face to Face, a story about a priest who takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Face to Face is a Bergman film title, but here it is a description. Confronté is a heraldic term.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry confronté describes two creatures placed facing each other, which is face to face.

clue.text: Smelly creature? Eluted runs

indicators.note: colours that run spread and lose their shape, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: something whiffy has been washed out and drained away.
explanation.walkthrough: Eluted is a lab word for washed out of a column, which fits 'runs' as a liquid; really runs signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The teledu is the stink badger of Java and Sumatra, which sprays a foul-smelling secretion when threatened.

clue.text: Bits of gut fitted upon a fiddle? Flip these perhaps

definitions.text: Bits of gut fitted upon a fiddle? Flip these perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: Bits of gut fitted upon a fiddle?
blocks.note: surface reading: catgut strings, the bits of gut stretched on a violin
setter's reading: real sections of the intestine, which a flip, a drink of beaten egg and liquor, passes through

explanation.walkthrough: The gut of violin strings is the false trail; the answer is anatomical, the parts of the small intestine just below the stomach. The parse of the fiddle part is not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodena are the first sections of the small intestine, literally bits of the gut.

clue.text: What's half-hewn, cut by chopper? It's easily penetrated

indicators.note: half of a word means only one of its two halves survives
a word cut by something is split open with that thing set in the gap

blocks.note: taken as written; its second half is kept
an axe is a chopping tool

explanation.surface: A woodcutting riddle: something half chopped, split by an axe, is soft and easy to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the back half of hewn is used, and the axe goes between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxen means soft like wax, yielding readily to pressure, so a waxen thing is easily pierced.

clue.text: 'Nun wife, New Church admitted' — Herald (second leader)

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so those letters go into the surrounding word

blocks.note: a Poor Clare is a nun of the Franciscan order founded by St Clare
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England
ux. is the abbreviation of Latin uxor, wife

explanation.surface: A news headline about a nun and a wife admitted to a new church, from the Herald newspaper's second leader column.
explanation.walkthrough: Herald looks like a newspaper and 'second leader' like its editorial; Clarenceux is one of England's heralds, second in rank among the Kings of Arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarenceux King of Arms is a senior officer of the College of Arms, ranking second after Garter.

clue.text: Old armour concealed by targe — a rerebrace?

indicators.note: concealed by says the answer lies tucked inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of targe, the word a, and the start of rerebrace

explanation.surface: An armour question: is a rerebrace, the plate for the upper arm, hidden behind a targe, a small round shield?
explanation.walkthrough: GEARE is an old spelling of gear, used in the sense of armour or harness; the hidden letters straddle three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear once meant a fighting man's equipment, armour included, and GEARE is that word's archaic spelling.

clue.text: Peer, sporty lord in the capacity of lecturer

blocks.note: Lord Coe, better known as Sebastian Coe, the Olympic middle-distance runner
qua is Latin for in the capacity of, used in English
L is a standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A peer of the realm, an athletic lord, appearing as a guest lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a member of the House of Lords, which the 'sporty lord' seems to continue; it is really an equal. Sebastian Coe, a British Olympic runner, became Lord Coe.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer in the sense of an equal is someone of the same rank, which is exactly what a coequal is.

clue.text: Came across work about pain-killer

blocks.note: to come across someone is to meet them; past tense
OP is short for opus, a work
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on a piece of writing about a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container instruction but here simply supplies ON, as in a book on birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Metopon is an opium-derived narcotic drug used medically to relieve pain.

clue.text: Sort of chalcedony: cut pure one after a short time (10, two words)

indicators.note: a cut word has its tail chopped off, losing the final letter
after says the pieces named before it are placed second, following the brief time

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
chaste means pure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jeweller's instruction: take a pure stone and cut it after a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha stone is a moss agate, a kind of chalcedony with dark branching markings.

clue.text: Mum has injected neat stuff for arthritic pain

indicators.note: something injected is pushed inside, so the second word goes inside the first

blocks.note: a familiar word for mother
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: Mother has given herself a shot of undiluted spirit to deal with her rheumatism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as undiluted drink but is the old word for cattle, here an ox.
explanation.definitionFit: Moxa is a downy plant material burnt on the skin as a traditional remedy, notably for gout and other joint pain.

clue.text: Hollywood types? Upset as none's found round set

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
found round says the rearranged letters are placed around the next word

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Film people are disappointed to find no one around the film set.
explanation.walkthrough: Set looks like a film set, but it means to solidify. Hollywood is a district of Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelenos are inhabitants of Los Angeles, which includes Hollywood, so its residents are examples.

clue.text: Guard guitar favoured by the stars

blocks.note: first meaning: a protective bar or panel, such as a fireguard or a car's wing
second meaning: the electric guitar brand played by many famous rock musicians

explanation.surface: A guard's guitar, the instrument famous performers prefer.
explanation.walkthrough: The stars are rock stars, not the night sky; Fender is the make of the Stratocaster and Telecaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a protective guard, and Fender is also the American maker of electric guitars used by countless celebrities.

clue.text: Know about brass that may be attached to the lobes

definitions.text: that may be attached to the lobes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word's letters go around the second's

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to know or study
brass and lip both mean cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Talk of knowing about brass ornaments worn on the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like metal for earrings, but it means nerve, as does lip.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip-on is an earring fastened by a clip, so it attaches to ear lobes without piercing.

clue.text: Organic compound to eat around start of evening

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone
around says the first part goes round the letter taken next

blocks.note: to dine is to eat
the opening letter of evening

explanation.surface: A chemist's dinner: an organic compound to eat around nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A diene is a hydrocarbon molecule containing two carbon-carbon double bonds, an organic chemical.

clue.text: Huge

blocks.note: reading one: a bare definition, enormous or immense
reading two: there is no wordplay, because this is the word readers write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This is Azed's competition clue: the word is given by a bare definition and readers send in their own clues for it. The crossing letters settle the O spelling over the variant with U.
explanation.definitionFit: Humongous is informal, originally American slang for something extremely large, so it is a plain synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: It's more than one pitch wherein you see chap unhappy about runs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for unhappy goes round the next abbreviation

blocks.note: a chap is a man
sad means unhappy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: several pitches where a man is upset about the runs scored.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch suggests a cricket pitch, but it is the slope of a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansard roof has two slopes on each side, the lower steeper than the upper, so more than one pitch.

clue.text: Having sauce with writers expects Scotch

blocks.note: sauce and lip both mean cheek or impudence
pens are writing implements

explanation.surface: A cheeky author looks forward to a glass of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky, but it labels the definition as a Scots word; lippen means to trust or count on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippen is a Scots verb meaning to trust or depend on, so lippens means expects, in Scots usage.

clue.text: What's mined open-cast one enters with narrow aperture

indicators.note: ground that is mined is dug up and broken apart, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mining talk: an opencast pit where a worker squeezes in through a tight gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The I enters the letters of open-cast before they are all rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenopaic describes something with a narrow slit or small opening, from the Greek for narrow and opening.

clue.text: Sobriquet 'Gentle' encapsulates forward

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so the word for gentle holds the next one inside

blocks.note: tame means docile, gentle
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A nickname, the Gentle one, captures something pushy about its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Toname is a Scots word for a nickname or byname, which is what a sobriquet is.

clue.text: Glass-maker's rod not broken in confusion

indicators.note: broken things are smashed into pieces, so the letters before it are rearranged
in says the rearranged letters go inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
pie is printers' term for a jumbled heap of type, so confusion

explanation.surface: A glassblower's rod has survived the mess unbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not broken' reads as intact, but broken alone is the signal and not is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontie, also pontil or punty, is the iron rod a glassblower uses to hold molten glass while shaping it.

clue.text: Guitar went lower before oboe's entry

indicators.note: an entry is where something comes in first, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: past tense of sink, to go down
the opening letter of oboe

explanation.surface: In an orchestra, the guitar dropped in pitch just before the oboe came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guitar' seems to be the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition; the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanko is a stringed instrument of West Africa, a kind of guitar or harp-lute.

clue.text: Modesty in statement from char when coming round?

indicators.note: a statement is something said out loud, so the answer matches the words as spoken

blocks.note: a charwoman arriving to clean might say this in dialect, I does meaning I do the cleaning

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady arrives and modestly says her piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a cleaning woman, who does for her employer; the answer is a Greek word, so the sound match is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidos is the Greek word for modesty, shame or reverence, personified as a goddess.

clue.text: Hamlet, old-style? Rep to get excited about opening thereof

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and stirred about into a new order
about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the opening letter of Hamlet, which thereof points back to

explanation.surface: A repertory actor gets worked up about the opening of Hamlet, played in old-fashioned style.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's play, but it means a small village. Thereof means 'of Hamlet', so its opening is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorp or thorpe is an old word for a village or hamlet, surviving in English place names.

clue.text: Spades carrying stiff coarse hemp

blocks.note: hard means stiff, unyielding
S is the abbreviation for spades, the card suit

explanation.surface: Workers with spades dig out tough coarse hemp.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue S carrying HARD means S sits underneath, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hards are the coarse refuse fibres of flax or hemp, separated in combing.

clue.text: Infusion: it's one favoured by earlier generations

blocks.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is
ane is an old and Scots form of one; like 'tis, a form older generations used

explanation.surface: A herbal tea is praised as the drink our grandparents preferred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favoured by earlier generations' looks like praise for herbal tea but marks the old-fashioned forms 'tis and ane.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, made by steeping leaves or flowers in hot water, which is an infusion.

clue.text: Reminder of summer holiday in Hungary? The opposite — imme-diately forgotten

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
the opposite swaps which part goes inside, so the country goes within the reminder instead

blocks.note: a suntan is what a summer holiday leaves behind
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: A suntan from a summer holiday in Hungary fades almost at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the least certain part: than is an obsolete form of then, meaning immediately after; forgotten marks that it is no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Than was formerly used as a spelling of then, at that moment, a sense now lost from the language.

clue.text: Shetland estate one's left — trouble turning it round

indicators.note: turning it round means taking everything built so far and reading it backwards

blocks.note: L for left, a side one has
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A Shetland landowner leaves an estate, and the trouble is reversing that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' covers the whole of L followed by ADO, so all four letters are read backwards. Odal, or udal, land was held under the old Norse freehold tenure of Orkney and Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Odal is the Norse-derived term for land held outright by inheritance in Shetland and Orkney, so it names such an estate.

clue.text: Church portico showing northern craftsmanship — a bit of magic

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
art is skill or craft
a hex is a spell or curse

explanation.surface: A church porch displays fine northern workmanship that seems almost magical.
explanation.definitionFit: A narthex is the porch or vestibule at the west end of a church, an entrance area before the nave.

clue.text: Oriental litter, edge gripped by 12?

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so the first word goes within the second

blocks.note: twelve o'clock is noon; the number is not a reference to the clue numbered 12
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An eastern litter whose edge is held by whatever the answer to clue 12 is.
explanation.walkthrough: A number in a clue usually points to another clue, and 12-across is right there; here 12 is just midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A norimon is a Japanese litter or palanquin, a covered chair carried on poles.

clue.text: She represents chastity, a help when rebuffed

indicators.note: a rebuff pushes something back, so the phrase is read in reverse

blocks.note: a help is an aid, written as an aid

explanation.surface: A chaste woman is offered help and turns it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon, was a virgin goddess and so the classical emblem of chastity.

clue.text: Suppurating rednesses round opening of scar — it's knowing what to put on (10, two words)

definitions.text: it's knowing what to put on

indicators.note: a suppurating wound is festering and broken down, so these letters are disordered
the opening of a word is just its first letter
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first letter of scar

explanation.surface: A medical scene of inflamed red patches around a scar, oddly ending with advice about what to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what to put on' sounds like ointment for the sore, but means clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is a feel for choosing clothes that suit you, which is knowledge of what to wear.
